subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Kopi Luwak: The World's Most Controversial Coffee
description: A short lesson to help you apply Kopi Luwak: The World's Most Controversial Coffee.

hook.text: Kopi Luwak is coffee made from beans eaten and excreted by civet cats. It sells for $100–600 per pound.

buildup.text: The legend says digestive enzymes in the civet's gut break down proteins, reducing bitterness and creating a uniquely smooth cup.

discovery.text: Specialty tasters consistently rate Kopi Luwak as mediocre—smoothness increases but complexity disappears.

twist.text: Most commercial Kopi Luwak comes from caged civets force-fed coffee cherries. The 'wild-harvested' story is largely marketing.

climax.text: Animal welfare organizations have condemned the industry. The world's most expensive coffee has one of the worst ethical records.

punchline.text: Exotic, expensive, overhyped, and often cruel. Fame doesn't mean quality.

quiz.question: How do specialty professionals rate Kopi Luwak's taste?
options: Consistently mediocre — smooth but lacking complexity
